Attack Vector: The attacker placed the actual attack script on a remote server like discord, and also uses third-party websites to anonymously paste text or mount files
The attacker directly downloads the malicious sample from the remote server to execute on the victim's machine
The attacker collects user host information and sends it back to their specified URL. The attack is relatively simple and less harmful
The attacker reflects a shell on the user's machine to the attacker's host
The attacker uses ASCII encoding to obfuscate the script. The characters are converted into corresponding ASCII codes for simple obfuscation
The attacker uses base64 encoding to obfuscate the script. The malicious script or program is embedded into the py file through base64 encoding, and then executed by exec

The attacker uses the mahdienc obfuscation tool. This tool uses zlib.compress, base64.b16encode, base64.b32encode, base64.b64encode, marshal.dumps, hex, and Cpython encoding serialization methods to obfuscate Python code
The attacker uses the Pyobfuscate obfuscation tool. This tool uses the pycryptodome module to encrypt and obfuscate Python source code. The final result contains four layers of obfuscation
The attacker uses the Pyarmor obfuscation tool. This is a mature Python obfuscation tool that can bind obfuscated code to a specific machine and set the validity period of the obfuscated code
